newsitem.title: USA: U.S. denies report of Russia spying in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. denies report of Russia spying in Bosnia.

text.p: The Defence Department on Tuesday denied a report that Russian troops in Bosnia conducted electronic spying on U.S. headquarters there.
"This story just simply is not true," Capt. Mike Doubleday, a Pentagon spokesman, said at a briefing.

The Washington Times quoted unidentified U.S. defence sources as saying a Russian communications van near the U.S. headquarters at Tuzla was packed with electronic eavesdropping gear to spy on U.S. operations.
It quoted one source as saying that when a U.S. officer tried to inspect the van, a Russian soldier threatened him with an AK-47 assault rifle.
Doubleday said it was only a communications van, there were no Russian guards in it and U.S. officers had access to it.
